d1: The node’s binding asks whether the edited image has a chalk-drawing appearance, but its pass criterion treats any convincing chalk-like rendering as complete fulfillment. The traces consistently cite grain, smudging, softened outlines, and sketch-like shading; the image does show those changes, yet retains photographic detail and color, so those cues alone do not establish that the requested transformation is fully complete. Make the decision criterion explicitly compare the edit with the source and distinguish visible progress toward chalk from a sufficiently complete chalk-made drawing, without prescribing a label or inventing medium-specific requirements. Keep unresolved for genuinely insufficient visual evidence. The single unknown trace is an API transport failure, not negative visual evidence; do not tune the visual criterion around it. Repeated high-confidence passes are a signal to investigate this criterion/label mismatch, not proof that the edit is absent.
